summary: Deep-dived the actual line-build content (tasks/steps/appliance/cook-time/sub-step quantities) behind the 4 Multi-usage and 12 Multi-version items to assess whether both toggles can be retired in favor of regular multi-task line builds. Multi versions vs options (steak doneness, burger bun/cheese/patty) looks fully redundant with existing task-level mapping_option — recommend deprecating it. Is Multi-usage qty Item is genuinely needed for Di Fara Pizza (topping oz scales inversely with topping count: 8oz to 6oz to 4oz, a count-based aggregate rule regular option-value mapping cannot express) but the 2 Smash Burger items using the same toggle show IDENTICAL content across their 2 tiers, suggesting misconfigured/unnecessary usage there. Also found the 18-line-build count on the main pizza item is ~90% restaurant-specific override duplication (77 distinct restaurants) layered on only 3-4 genuine quantity tiers, a separate complexity source from the toggle itself.
questions: Company-wide, how many other is_multiple_usage=true items follow the burger pattern (redundant/no-op tiers) vs the pizza pattern (genuine count-based quantity need)?
learned: Multi versions vs options duplicates the standard multi-task + mapping_option line-build capability already used for regular items — same option-value branching, just packaged as separate line-build objects instead of parallel tasks in one line build.

Is Multi-usage qty Item solves a genuinely different problem (ingredient quantity keyed to COUNT of selected multi-select values, not to a specific value) that standard per-option-value task mapping cannot express without combinatorial blowup — real usage is currently just 1 item family (Di Fara Pizza + its pilot clone).
thinking: If leadership wants to eliminate the multi-usage pattern too, the right replacement is a formula/scaled-quantity field on the BOM line (quantity as a function of selection count) rather than forcing regular single-line-build config, since regular config cannot express the aggregate-count dependency.
followups: Audit all is_multiple_usage=true items company-wide to separate genuine-need cases from redundant/misconfigured ones before deciding scope of deprecation
If Multi versions vs options is deprecated, plan migration of the 12 affected items to multi-task line builds with mapping_option per task
